purpose: Configuration benchmarks for the controls that cite neither CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations nor CISA ScubaGear in controls.json. relations.Stricter: The control passes only when the item passes, and can fail where the item passes.

AAD-1.2.ItemTitle: Microsoft Entra ID must be configured to use multifactor authentication (MFA).
AAD-1.2.Why: The check verifies a Conditional Access MFA policy whose state is On with 'All users' included and any user exclusions documented with the AO; the fix grants 'Require multifactor authentication' on All cloud apps. Satisfied requires an enabled policy including All users on All cloud apps that requires MFA (or an authentication strength, which requires MFA), with no exclusions or only exclusions on the tenant's approval record, and is stricter on apps, client types and registration.
AAD-1.2.Unchecked: Whether the exclusion approval is documented with the authorizing official: the tool's EmergencyAccess record names an approver and dates but cannot establish that the approver is the AO, so an approved exclusion passes here and still needs the AO documentation the STIG check asks for.

AAD-11.3.ItemId: All risky workload identities are triaged (Zero Trust Assessment test 21862)
AAD-11.3.ItemTitle: All risky workload identities are triaged
AAD-11.3.Why: Microsoft's check fails when identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals returns any service principal with riskState 'atRisk' (or any servicePrincipalRiskDetection is atRisk). The evaluator reads the same collection and is Satisfied only when none is atRisk (it also fails on confirmedCompromised, which the check does not), so Satisfied passes that half of the check.
AAD-11.3.Unchecked: The check's second half, identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections with riskState 'atRisk', is not read; an untriaged detection on a principal whose aggregate state is not atRisk would fail the check and pass here.

AAD-14.1.ItemId: Application certificates must be rotated on a regular basis (Zero Trust Assessment test 21992)
AAD-14.1.ItemTitle: Application certificates must be rotated on a regular basis
AAD-14.1.Why: Microsoft: 'Query all of your service principals and application registrations that have certificate credentials. Make sure the certificate start date is less than 180 days' (test 21992 fails on a keyCredential whose startDateTime is more than 180 days ago). For app registrations, Satisfied requires every certificate to be unexpired with more than 30 days left and a lifetime of 180 days or less, so its start date is less than 150 days ago and the app-registration half of the check passes.
AAD-14.1.Unchecked: Certificate credentials on service principals (the check queries both applications and servicePrincipals keyCredentials); the collector reads /applications only.

AAD-3.4.ItemId: Step 6: Configure PIM > Configure activation settings > 'Require justification'
AAD-3.4.ItemTitle: For each privileged role ... Configure settings: Require justification
AAD-3.4.Why: The guide's step sets 'Require justification' on the PIM activation settings of each privileged role, which is the Justification entry in the role policy's Enablement_EndUser_Assignment rule the evaluator reads; Satisfied means every policy for the 17 roles the tool treats as privileged (which include Microsoft's stated minimum set: Global, Privileged Role, Security, Exchange and SharePoint Administrator) has it.
AAD-3.4.Unchecked: Roles the organization identifies as privileged beyond the tool's fixed 17-role list (for example Hybrid Identity Administrator or custom roles) are not judged when the policy-to-role map is available. The other settings in the same step (require MFA, maximum duration, approval) are separate controls (AAD-3.3, AAD-3.6, AAD-3.5).

DNS-1.4.ItemTitle: Receiving domains should implement protocols to signal TLS usage to clients. Receivers should implement DANE, MTA-STS (or both) for all mail servers listed in the domain's MX Resource Record set.
DNS-1.4.Why: A published MTA-STS record with a retrievable policy in enforce mode is MTA-STS implemented for the domain; enforce is the mode in which, per Section 5.2.5 Table 5-2, a client rejects the connection on a TLS validation or MX matching failure.
DNS-1.4.Unchecked: That the policy's mx: entries cover every host in the domain's MX RR set and that each MX host presents a certificate matching them; max_age; domains not in the assessed DNS domain list. (DANE alone also passes the recommendation, where DNS-1.4 would report a Gap.)

DNS-1.6.ItemTitle: Organizations should deploy DNSSEC for all DNS name servers and validate DNSSEC responses from all systems that receive email.
DNS-1.6.Why: A DS record at the parent (or a signed enclosing zone) shows the domain's zone is DNSSEC-signed and delegated securely, which is the deploy-DNSSEC half of the recommendation for that domain.
DNS-1.6.Unchecked: DNSSEC validation by the organization's receiving mail systems (Exchange Online's validation is Microsoft's); that the signatures actually validate (a DS with broken signatures still passes); domains not in the assessed list.

DNS-2.1.ItemId: Section 4.5.3, Table 4-3 'Recommended Cryptographic Key Parameters' (RSA/SHA-256 row)

DNS-2.1.Why: On the lifetime column, DNS-2.1's 365-day limit is within the 1-2 year recommended lifetime, so every Satisfied key passes it (stricter on that part).
DNS-2.1.Unchecked: The recommended 2048-bit length (judged by EXO-1.4 and shown here only as context) and the RSA/SHA-256 algorithm (Security Recommendation 4-3).

AAD-10.4.Reason: The evaluator accepts any enabled policy with any interval and any scope. Near-misses that fail the rule: Zero Trust Assessment checks 'Privileged users have short-lived sign-in sessions' (test 21825: every privileged role covered by an enabled policy with sign-in frequency 4 hours or less) and 'Guests don't have long lived sign-in sessions' (test 21824: a policy targeting guests or external users at 24 hours or less, 1 day, or every time) - a 30-day frequency on one group is Satisfied here and fails both. DISA STIG V-270200 (session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity) is a different setting (idle session timeout), not sign-in frequency. ScubaGear 2.0.0 has no sign-in frequency rule.
AAD-10.4.EarnBy: Add a per-population judgment: for each privileged role, an enabled policy including that role with signInFrequency type hours and value 4 or less (cite ZTA 21825), and for guests an enabled policy with includeGuestsOrExternalUsers and 24 hours or less (cite ZTA 21824). The collector would need to store signInFrequency.type and .value.

AAD-11.2.Reason: Closest item: Microsoft Zero Trust check 'Guests are not assigned high privileged directory roles' (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/zero-trust-protect-tenants#guests-are-not-assigned-high-privileged-directory-roles; Zero Trust Assessment test 22128, which fails on any user with userType 'Guest' holding a role whose roleDefinition.isPrivileged is true, active or eligible). It fails the rule on two counts: the evaluator identifies guests by '#EXT#' in the UPN, not by userType, so a userType=Guest account without '#EXT#' (a member converted to guest, or one created as Guest through Graph) holding Global Administrator is Satisfied here and fails the check; and the tool's fixed 18-role list is narrower than Microsoft's isPrivileged set (for example Hybrid Identity Administrator, Domain Name Administrator, External Identity Provider Administrator, Password Administrator), so a guest in one of those roles is Satisfied here and fails the check. ScubaGear 2.0.0 and the DISA Entra ID STIG V1R1 have no guest-in-role rule.
AAD-11.2.EarnBy: Have the roles collector add userType to the principal read and the role definitions' isPrivileged property (Graph v1.0 unifiedRoleDefinition), then flag any principal with userType 'Guest' (keep '#EXT#' as an additional signal) in any role with isPrivileged true, permanent or eligible. That makes it Equivalent to ZTA 22128 (stricter where '#EXT#' members are also flagged).

ScubaGear 2.0.0 and the DISA STIG have no token-protection rule.

AAD-11.9.Reason: Closest item: Microsoft Zero Trust check 'Workload Identities are configured with risk-based policies' (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/zero-trust-response-remediation#workload-identities-are-configured-with-risk-based-policies), whose remediation is 'Create a risk-based Conditional Access policy for workload identities'. AAD-12.2.Reason: Closest item: Microsoft Zero Trust check 'Inactive guest identities are disabled or removed from the tenant' (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/zero-trust-protect-tenants#inactive-guest-identities-are-disabled-or-removed-from-the-tenant; test 21858: fails on any enabled guest whose lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime, or creation date when none, is more than 90 days ago).
